description: We’re LunaLupa, a team from Thrissur, Kerala, building a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer—a playful web game where young learners experience astronaut training through docking, spacewalk safety, Moon exploration, and emergency drills. Our prototype combines fun gameplay with verified NASA facts, badges, and graduation certificates. We aim to expand with Artemis and Mars missions. We welcome teammates skilled in coding, AI, UI/UX, animation, game design, and educational storytelling!
summary:
LunaLupa: The Last Signal is an interactive lunar mission simulation that challenges players to guide a four-member astronaut crew through a mission to the Moon's south pole.

Players assemble their crew, begin the mission, explore lunar landing conditions, and make decisions as the mission progresses. The experience introduces learners to the challenges of lunar exploration, including terrain assessment, crew coordination, and managing a lunar outpost.

The project incorporates NASA's Moon Trek as a real-world lunar terrain reference, connecting an educational simulation with authentic NASA lunar exploration resources. Simplified terrain risk ratings are used for gameplay and are not presented as actual NASA measurements.

LunaLupa aims to make space science more engaging, encourage critical thinking, and inspire young people to explore the challenges of human spaceflight.
details:
LunaLupa: The Last Signal is a browser-based lunar survival simulation developed to make space exploration more interactive and accessible to young learners.

The game follows a four-member astronaut crew arriving at the Moon to establish an outpost. Players progress through six mission stages: terrain reconnaissance, lunar landing, life-support management, radiation storm response, food production, and investigation of a mysterious signal.

Each stage presents a mission situation in which players must consider possible risks and make decisions. The experience introduces concepts such as lunar terrain, astronaut safety, resource management, and the challenges of maintaining a lunar habitat.

NASA Moon Trek is used as a reference for lunar surface exploration. The game translates the idea of examining craters, slopes, and landing conditions into simplified gameplay choices. The risk levels and resource effects are illustrative game mechanics, not actual NASA measurements or a live NASA data feed.

The project was developed using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. It is an independent educational prototype designed to encourage curiosity about space science, critical thinking, and interest in STEM.

LunaLupa is an educational simulation and is not an operational astronaut-training system or an official NASA product.
